rows.best_cross_checks: Power/cooling envelope, procurement/RMA records, scheduler node lists, BMC inventory, switch topology, external construction/utility data.
rows.key_value_ranges_encodings: Accelerator count: 0-site max. H100e-equivalent capacity: 0+ normalized chips or sustained FLOP/s. GPU memory: 0-SKU max GB. Power cap: 0-TDP W. MIG/vGPU/MPS: enum off/on/profile. Topology: graph; low-latency domain size 1, 8, 72, etc. Health counters: 0+ counts; spikes indicate failures or hidden stress.
rows.large_training_signature_interpretation: Capacity signal, not activity. Strong precondition if many homogeneous high-end accelerators are connected by low-latency GPU and scale-out fabric and backed by sufficient power/cooling. Widespread partitioning into small MIG/vGPU slices usually weakens large synchronous-training feasibility unless reconfigured.
rows.main_false_negatives_failure_modes: Undeclared hardware, stale inventory, off-ledger swaps, hidden clusters, inaccurate sustained-efficiency assumptions, treating raw chip count as stable across generations.
rows.main_false_positives: Large inference fleet, HPC simulation fleet, idle reserved capacity, cloud burst capacity, mixed-generation inventory.
rows.precise_data_objects: GPU SKU/model, count, UUID/serial where available, PCI bus ID, host/node/rack/pod/site, HBM capacity, precision modes, peak Tensor Core capability, TDP/power cap, MIG/vGPU/MPS/sharing status, driver/CUDA/firmware/VBIOS/NCCL, application clocks, persistence/performance state, NVLink/NVSwitch/PCIe/NIC/NUMA topology, ECC/retired-pages/row-remap/XID/PCIe replay/NVLink errors, replacement/RMA logs.
rows.primary_governance_function: Shows what the site could physically do; normalizes all other signals by chip generation, topology, and power/cooling envelope. Not evidence of an active run by itself.
rows.recommended_reporting_form: Signed hourly/daily pseudonymized inventory snapshot; public aggregate only by broad chip class and capacity band; raw serials only under inspection.
rows.sensitivity: High: reveals strategic capacity, export-control-relevant facts, tenancy layout, redundancy, and procurement timing.

rows.access_feasibility_1_5: 5 for managed/HPC clusters; 3-4 for clouds after aggregation
rows.best_cross_checks: GPU telemetry, fabric collectives, power, storage checkpointing, cloud billing/API logs, runtime metadata.
rows.key_value_ranges_encodings: Allocated GPUs: 0-site max. Duration: seconds-months. GPU-hours: GPUs×hours, 0+. Concurrency fraction: allocated GPUs / available GPUs, 0-1. Homogeneity: fraction of one SKU/topology, 0-1. Reservation length: hours-182+ days depending system. Declaration class: enum train/fine-tune/inference/HPC/unknown.
rows.large_training_signature_interpretation: One or linked jobs reserving hundreds to thousands+ of homogeneous accelerators for many hours/days/weeks, high concurrency fraction, contiguous topology, stable membership, few preemptions, and training-like runtime/image labels. Absence of such allocations is strong negative evidence only if scheduler coverage is complete.
rows.main_false_negatives_failure_modes: Actor splits across accounts/jobs/time, runs on unmanaged hosts, masks declarations, uses multiple providers, uses many small jobs orchestrated externally.
rows.main_false_positives: HPC simulations, large batch inference/synthetic data, stress tests, benchmark runs, large data analytics, rendering.
rows.observable: Scheduler, job, reservation, and allocation metadata
rows.precise_data_objects: Job/account/project IDs, batch job or K8s pod/Ray/Slurm job IDs, workflow/reservation IDs, submit/start/end times, elapsed/wall duration, allocated GPU count/type, node list, rack/pod/fabric locality, queue/partition/priority/preemption state, TRES/GRES/GPU-hours/node-hours/energy, declared workload type, expected FLOPs/duration, container/VM image digest, command/env hash, mounted volume/bucket IDs, dataset/checkpoint declarations.
rows.primary_governance_function: Best first-pass signal in a managed cluster: identifies candidate windows, concurrency, duration, allocation boundaries, job/account linkage, and declared workload class.
rows.recommended_reporting_form: Pseudonymized job graph with hashed identities, broad workload class, GPU-hours, topology band, and delay; raw job command only under trigger.
rows.sensitivity: Very high: exposes customers, projects, business relationships, model-development timing, data locations, and command fingerprints.

rows.access_feasibility_1_5: 4 for provider/regulator; 2 for customers only within account
rows.best_cross_checks: Scheduler allocations, EFA/RDMA fabric traffic, billing continuity, GPU power, storage egress, declarations.
rows.key_value_ranges_encodings: API event counts: 0+ per minute/hour. Instance count: 0-provider quota. Reservation size: 1-N instances; public AWS Capacity Blocks support fixed counts/durations for supported instance families. Duration: minutes-182 days in some reservation products. Billing: 0+ currency/hour; continuity/diurnal index 0-1.
rows.large_training_signature_interpretation: Large synchronized provisioning or reservation of high-end training instance types, cluster placement/EFA/RDMA, continuous billing for days/weeks, high GPU-hour spend, correlated teardown after training window. Strong attribution because identity and payment trail are attached.
rows.main_false_negatives_failure_modes: Fragmentation across accounts/providers/regions, on-premise bare metal, resale/managed-service indirection, spot/preemptible fragmentation, under-threshold splitting.
rows.main_false_positives: Reserved inference capacity, stress tests, customer benchmark campaigns, HPC burst, disaster recovery warm pools.
rows.observable: Cloud control-plane, capacity reservation, and billing records
rows.precise_data_objects: Create/start/stop/terminate instance events, instance type/SKU, region/AZ/placement group, IAM principal/API caller/account, launch template, EFA/RDMA options, capacity reservations/blocks, reservation start/end/duration/instance count, usage line items, GPU-hour or instance-hour billing, cost allocation tags, egress/network charges.
rows.primary_governance_function: Shows who provisioned what, when, in which region/AZ, and how long it was paid for; highly useful for clouds and multi-tenant providers.
rows.recommended_reporting_form: Regulator receives account-pseudonymized capacity and usage bands; raw IAM and billing only after trigger.
rows.sensitivity: High: commercial relationships, costs, account identity, procurement timing, regional strategy.

rows.access_feasibility_1_5: 5 on self-managed; 3-4 in managed clouds; lower under confidential modes
rows.best_cross_checks: Scheduler, scale-out fabric periodicity, power, runtime metadata, storage checkpointing, monitoring-integrity logs.
rows.key_value_ranges_encodings: Utilization/SM/tensor active: 0-100%. HBM used: 0-SKU capacity GB or 0-100%. Power: 0-TDP W or 0-100% of cap. Clocks: 0-SKU max MHz. Temperature: ambient to throttle threshold. Errors: 0+ counts. Per-process memory: 0-HBM GB.
rows.large_training_signature_interpretation: Many GPUs show sustained high SM/tensor activity, high but stable HBM residency, high power fraction, synchronized cycles, and few idle gaps over long windows. By itself it says “heavy GPU compute,” not necessarily training.
rows.main_false_negatives_failure_modes: Counter disabled, CC-On modes, sampling too coarse, workload throttled or intentionally underutilized, process accounting off, aggregation hides small high-intensity subsets.
rows.main_false_positives: Large batch inference, synthetic-data generation, HPC dense linear algebra, burn-in tests, crypto/other high compute, memory-bound inference with high HBM use.
rows.observable: On-device GPU telemetry: utilization, memory, power, health, process accounting
rows.precise_data_objects: GPU busy/utilization %, SM active %, Tensor Core/pipe activity if exposed, memory copy utilization, framebuffer/HBM used/free, memory temperature and bandwidth proxy, PCIe/NVLink TX/RX, board/module power and energy, clocks/P-states, throttle reasons, ECC/XID/row-remap/PCIe replay/NVLink errors, per-process PID/name/memory/utilization/accounting if enabled.
rows.primary_governance_function: Shows whether allocated accelerators were actually busy, synchronized, memory-resident, power-drawing, and healthy; distinguishes idle reservation from active computation.
rows.recommended_reporting_form: Per-job or per-pseudonymous-node time series at 1-60s cadence with process names hashed; raw process info under trigger.
rows.sensitivity: Medium-high: workload fingerprints, customer process names, model size hints, performance tuning details.

rows.best_cross_checks: GPU utilization/power, runtime metadata, NCCL/fabric traffic, ML logs if available.
rows.key_value_ranges_encodings: Counters usually 0-100% active, 0+ launches/sec, 0+ bytes/sec, 0-peak throughput. Kernel-name field should be hashed/redacted. Sampling cadence milliseconds-minutes. Availability enum: available/disabled/blocked-by-security-mode.
rows.large_training_signature_interpretation: High Tensor Core activity, repeated forward/backward/optimizer kernel sequence, stable step periodicity, and distributed collective adjacency. Stronger than raw GPU utilization when available, but still not definitive without scheduler/fabric/runtime context.
rows.main_false_negatives_failure_modes: Profiling disabled, insufficient sampling, counter virtualization, confidential-compute modes disabling performance counters, kernel obfuscation or fused kernels.
rows.main_false_positives: Benchmarking, HPC ML-like solvers, batched inference, synthetic data generation, vendor burn-in.
rows.precise_data_objects: Kernel launch counts, kernel name hashes, tensor/matrix instruction activity, achieved occupancy, achieved FLOP/s or throughput proxy, memory bandwidth, stall reasons, cache metrics, profiler session metadata, CUPTI/DCGM profiling fields, enabled/disabled mode, sample cadence.
rows.primary_governance_function: Reveals computation mix, kernel classes, Tensor Core use, memory/compute bottlenecks, and sometimes framework fingerprints; useful for distinguishing training-like kernels from generic utilization.
rows.recommended_reporting_form: Only aggregated activity classes and hashed kernel families; raw traces under inspection order.
rows.sensitivity: Very high: can reveal model architecture, framework, kernels, and performance trade secrets.

rows.access_feasibility_1_5: 4 on supported systems; 2-3 where counters are not surfaced
rows.best_cross_checks: Scale-out fabric, scheduler node lists, runtime WORLD_SIZE/rank mapping, GPU SM activity.
rows.key_value_ranges_encodings: Link utilization: 0-100% of physical link. Aggregate domain bandwidth: 0-domain max. Link state: up/down/degraded. Errors/recoveries: 0+ counts. Domain size: 1-SKU/system max. Correlation between GPU links: -1 to 1.
rows.large_training_signature_interpretation: High recurring GPU-GPU traffic across many peers, synchronized with compute steps, especially inside 8-GPU nodes or 72-GPU NVLink domains. Tensor/model parallel training tends to stress local fabric more than simple data-parallel-only runs.
rows.main_false_negatives_failure_modes: Data-parallel training with limited local traffic, counters disabled, coarse aggregation, use of PCIe/NIC path instead of NVLink, topology hiding.
rows.main_false_positives: Multi-GPU inference with tensor parallelism, HPC collectives, benchmarks, model serving with large context/KV sharding.
rows.observable: Intra-node GPU fabric: NVLink/NVSwitch/PCIe peer traffic
rows.precise_data_objects: Per-link TX/RX bytes, aggregate NVLink bandwidth, link state/up/down, recovery/replay/error counters, NVSwitch fabric membership, clique/fabric/domain IDs, NVSwitch port counters and power, PCIe peer traffic, topology graph.
rows.primary_governance_function: Shows whether GPUs inside nodes or NVLink/NVSwitch domains are communicating in training-like collectives or tensor/model parallel patterns.
rows.recommended_reporting_form: Aggregate per-domain utilization/correlation and errors; no raw topology beyond pseudonymous domains unless triggered.
rows.sensitivity: Medium-high: topology and model-parallel strategy are commercially sensitive.

rows.best_cross_checks: Scheduler, GPU utilization, power, runtime rank count, storage checkpointing, host process metadata.
rows.category: Primary activity / concurrency and synchronization signal
rows.key_value_ranges_encodings: Port utilization: 0-100% line rate. Packet/drop/retry/error counters: 0+. Latency: microseconds-milliseconds. Cross-port correlation: -1 to 1. Periodicity: seconds-minutes. Burst duty cycle: 0-1. Synchronized-fabric footprint: 1-N ports/nodes.
rows.large_training_signature_interpretation: Hundreds/thousands of ports show periodic correlated bursts, all-reduce/all-gather/reduce-scatter-like traffic, high utilization during collectives, barrier-like congestion, and stable step cadence. Absence of such patterns during claimed large training is strong negative evidence.
rows.main_false_negatives_failure_modes: Coarse sampling that misses bursts, application-level traffic shaping, hierarchical/offloaded collectives, cross-provider splitting, encrypted/opaque overlays, missing job-port mapping.
rows.main_false_positives: MPI/HPC simulations, distributed storage rebuilds, large data movement, all-to-all analytics, benchmark collectives.
rows.precise_data_objects: Per-switch/port bytes, packets, utilization, RDMA sends/receives, queue-pair/flow summaries, ECN/PFC, drops, retransmits, XmitWait/congestion, latency histograms, link errors, job-to-port mapping, cluster/fabric partitions, telemetry cadence and counter resets.
rows.primary_governance_function: Most distinctive non-semantic signal for large distributed training: reveals synchronized collective communication across many nodes.
rows.recommended_reporting_form: Per-job/pseudonymous-fabric aggregate features: footprint, utilization bands, periodicity, congestion/error summaries; raw flow logs only under trigger.
rows.sensitivity: High: reveals cluster topology, workload timing, model-parallel strategy, customer tenancy, and bottlenecks.

rows.best_cross_checks: GPU telemetry, scheduler allocation, cooling, facility limits, fabric collectives.
rows.category: Secondary/primary corroboration; hard-to-fake physical activity signal
rows.key_value_ranges_encodings: GPU power: 0-TDP W or 0-100% of cap. Server power: 0-nameplate kW. Rack power: 0-100+ kW depending design. Facility IT power: 0+ MW. Energy: kWh. Diurnal index/CV: 0-1+. Cadence: sub-second to hourly.
rows.large_training_signature_interpretation: Sustained high power across many homogeneous racks with low diurnal variation and synchronized or step-like fine-scale structure. Power cannot distinguish training from other heavy compute alone, but it is difficult to spoof when measured outside the host.
rows.main_false_negatives_failure_modes: Coarse metering, mixed workloads masking signal, intentional underclocking, shifted load to unmetered circuits, PUE/cooling confusion, missing rack-level mapping.
rows.main_false_positives: HPC, batch inference, burn-in, cryptocurrency or other dense compute, cooling/measurement artifacts.
rows.precise_data_objects: GPU board/module power, server/chassis BMC/IPMI/Redfish power, rack PDU outlet/feed, busway, UPS, transformer, utility meter, energy kWh, power-cap/throttle events, power anomalies, generator/backup transitions, measurement coverage and cadence.
rows.primary_governance_function: Independent physical confirmation of sustained accelerator load and capacity envelope; excellent for corroboration and negative certification.
rows.recommended_reporting_form: Rack/pod aggregate kW/kWh with pseudonymous mapping and coverage metadata; raw circuit maps under inspection.
rows.sensitivity: Medium-high: reveals capacity, utilization, costs, and site operations.

rows.best_cross_checks: Power, GPU temps/throttle, scheduler rack placement, facility PUE/IT-load model.
rows.key_value_ranges_encodings: Temperature: ambient to throttle threshold °C. Fan speed: 0-100% or RPM. Liquid flow: 0+ L/min. CDU delta-T: 0+ °C. Chiller/heat rejection: kW/MW. Thermal alarms: count/state. Cadence: seconds-minutes.
rows.large_training_signature_interpretation: Elevated stable heat load aligned with GPU power over days/weeks; high-density rack/pod operation; thermal throttling if cooling near limits. Cooling is slower and less semantically specific than power.
rows.main_false_negatives_failure_modes: Aggregation at facility level, thermal inertia smoothing bursts, lack of rack mapping, overbuilt cooling hiding signal.
rows.main_false_positives: Any sustained high-power workload, environmental heatwaves, cooling faults, maintenance, data movement/storage heat.
rows.precise_data_objects: GPU and HBM temperatures, server inlet/exhaust temperatures, fan speeds, CDU supply/return temperatures, liquid flow/pressure, valve states, heat rejection, chiller/plant load, leak/maintenance alarms, thermal throttling events, rack/pod thermal maps.
rows.primary_governance_function: Corroborates sustained high power, detects unreported high-density operation, and constrains feasibility of very large runs.
rows.recommended_reporting_form: Pod/rack aggregate heat-load and delta-T bands with coverage; raw maps under inspection.
rows.sensitivity: Medium: facility design, operational resilience, cooling technology, site constraints.

rows.access_feasibility_1_5: 4 self-managed; 2 public cloud guest-isolated; 3 with hashed metadata
rows.best_cross_checks: Scheduler job IDs, GPU process accounting, NCCL/fabric patterns, storage checkpointing, ML logs.
rows.category: Primary semantic / attribution signal, when accessible
rows.key_value_ranges_encodings: WORLD_SIZE/rank count: 1-N GPU processes. Local rank: 0-GPUs-per-node-1. Process memory: 0-HBM. Image hash: categorical. Framework class: enum. Rendezvous connections: 0-N. Runtime duration: seconds-months.
rows.large_training_signature_interpretation: Large WORLD_SIZE/rank count, distributed-training launchers, training frameworks, optimizer/checkpoint libraries, stable rank mapping, and containers linked to scheduler allocation. Very strong semantics if authentic; often unavailable in privacy-preserving clouds.
rows.main_false_negatives_failure_modes: Hash-only metadata, user-space hiding, encrypted launchers, container nesting, untrusted host, no guest visibility, external orchestration.
rows.main_false_positives: Distributed inference with tensor parallelism, HPC MPI jobs, synthetic data pipelines, ML benchmarks.
rows.observable: Host, VM, container, process, and distributed-runtime metadata
rows.precise_data_objects: Host kernel/driver/modules/cgroups, VM ID/image/hypervisor/placement/vCPU/RAM/accelerator mapping, container image digest/pod UID/namespace/labels/annotations/entrypoint hash, process tree/cmdline hash/user/PID-GPU mapping, CUDA/NCCL/cuDNN/PyTorch/JAX/TF/DeepSpeed/Megatron/vLLM/TensorRT versions, launcher logs, MASTER_ADDR/PORT, WORLD_SIZE/RANK/LOCAL_RANK, rendezvous and rank mapping, Ray/K8s/Slurm linkage.
rows.primary_governance_function: Connects physical activity to software identity: framework, image, process tree, distributed world size, ranks, rendezvous, and customer/application class.
rows.recommended_reporting_form: Hashes and normalized runtime classes by default; raw command/env/labels only under trigger and secret scrubbing.
rows.sensitivity: Very high: code, customer identity, model architecture, data paths, secrets in command lines if not scrubbed.

rows.access_feasibility_1_5: 3; many logs disabled/costly; 4 in controlled HPC
rows.best_cross_checks: Scheduler/runtime, power/GPU activity, checkpoint periodicity, cloud egress billing, ML logs.
rows.key_value_ranges_encodings: Bytes/request or per hour: 0-PB+. Operations/sec: 0+. File count: 0+. Checkpoint period: minutes-days. Checkpoint size: GB-TB+ depending model/sharding. Read/write ratio: 0-∞. Burst periodicity: none/regular/irregular. Prefix identity: hash.
rows.large_training_signature_interpretation: Large initial staging, repeated dataset shard reads, periodic checkpoint writes, optimizer-state-sized writes, checkpoint export/deletion after run, and storage bursts aligned with scheduler/fabric step or epoch boundaries.
rows.main_false_negatives_failure_modes: Streaming from local cache, checkpoint disabled/infrequent, logs disabled, encrypted or renamed prefixes, sharded checkpoints hidden in many small files, cross-provider fragmentation.
rows.main_false_positives: ETL/data lakes, backups, distributed storage rebuilds, large inference cache warmup, model serving rollouts, scientific datasets.
rows.observable: Storage, object-store, filesystem, and data-movement logs
rows.precise_data_objects: Object-store request logs, bucket/prefix hashes, operation type, requester/account/source IP/job, bytes read/written, request timestamps, lifecycle/deletion events, filesystem POSIX/MPI-IO/HDF5 summaries, metadata ops, file counts, IOPS, per-job I/O, checkpoint paths, retention/export, inter-region/cross-provider transfer, storage telemetry gaps.
rows.primary_governance_function: Detects dataset staging, repeated shard reads, checkpoint writes, model export, and training-adjacent data movement.
rows.recommended_reporting_form: Hashed prefixes, bytes/time bins, operation classes, per-job aggregates; raw path/object names only under trigger.
rows.sensitivity: Very high: dataset identity, model/checkpoint sizes, customer IP, research timeline.

rows.best_cross_checks: Scheduler, fabric, GPU telemetry, storage checkpoints, attestation/integrity, billing.
rows.key_value_ranges_encodings: Parameters: 10^6-10^13+. Tokens: 10^6-10^16+. Steps: 1-10^7. Batch/tokens per step: 1-10^9+. Loss: real-valued time series. Checkpoints: 0+ events. Declaration class: categorical; confidence signed/unsigned.
rows.large_training_signature_interpretation: Authentic logs showing high total tokens×parameters/compute, long distributed training, loss improvement, checkpoints, and model-development purpose are near-definitive. Use as escalation/declaration evidence rather than routine public telemetry.
rows.main_false_negatives_failure_modes: No access, deliberate non-logging, falsified declarations, fragmented training phases, confidential R&D objections.
rows.main_false_positives: Fabricated logs, benchmarks, toy runs with large declarations, post-training or eval logs mislabeled.
rows.observable: Workload declarations, experiment trackers, and ML training logs
rows.precise_data_objects: Declared purpose, model family/parameter count, precision, sequence length, dataset/token count, batch/global batch, optimizer and learning-rate schedule, step count, step time, loss curves, gradient norms, checkpoint metadata, experiment tracker runs, training/eval/inference logs, synthetic-data generation logs, signed declaration hashes.
rows.primary_governance_function: Directly describes whether a run is training, fine-tuning, inference, synthetic data, evaluation, or HPC; if trustworthy, the highest semantic value.
rows.recommended_reporting_form: Signed high-level declarations; raw logs only under protected audit; publish none or only aggregate compliance status.
rows.sensitivity: Extreme: core IP, model architecture, dataset, performance, safety work, customer secrets.

rows.best_cross_checks: Monitoring integrity, hardware inventory, GPU/fabric telemetry gaps, physical maintenance records.
rows.key_value_ranges_encodings: Attestation validity: true/false/expired. Measurement hash: categorical. CC/security mode: off/on/devtools/unknown. Counter availability: enabled/disabled. Signature verification: valid/invalid. Firmware delta: none/changed. Collector trust score: 0-1.
rows.large_training_signature_interpretation: Does not say training occurred. It says whether other evidence can be trusted. Counter-disabled secure modes can create a governance tradeoff: more confidentiality may reduce observability.
rows.main_false_negatives_failure_modes: Partial coverage, unverifiable switches/BMCs, trusted device but untrusted host, replayed tokens, opaque vendor modes, counters disabled in secure mode.
rows.main_false_positives: Valid attestation on idle or inference hardware; attestation only covers boot state, not workload.
rows.observable: Attestation, trusted computing, and device/telemetry provenance
rows.precise_data_objects: Device certificates/identity, manufacturer chain, firmware and driver measurements, secure/measured boot, TEE/confidential-compute mode, GPU attestation token/report, NVSwitch/fabric attestation where available, telemetry-agent binary hash, signed counter batches, key rotation, config changes, counter-disabled states.
rows.primary_governance_function: Indicates whether hardware, firmware, boot state, telemetry collectors, and security modes are authentic and unmodified; protects against falsified telemetry.
rows.recommended_reporting_form: Signed attestation status, measurement class, counter availability, and coverage; raw measurements to auditor only.
rows.sensitivity: Medium-high: platform configuration and security posture.

rows.best_cross_checks: Attestation, physical/security logs, power continuity, scheduler windows, cloud control-plane events.
rows.key_value_ranges_encodings: Coverage fraction: 0-1. Gap fraction: 0-1. Scrape interval: seconds-hours. Clock drift: ms-s. Reset count: 0+. Config change count: 0+. Signature validity: valid/invalid. Retention days: 0+. Coverage-by-layer vector.
rows.large_training_signature_interpretation: Integrity logs rarely prove training, but suspicious telemetry gaps during high-power/high-allocation windows increase suspicion. Complete, signed, synchronized coverage is mandatory for credible negative certification.
rows.main_false_negatives_failure_modes: Attacker compromises monitor, deletes or backfills logs, subtle sampling reduction, clock skew, unmonitored subclusters, retention expiration.
rows.main_false_positives: Benign outages, maintenance, collector upgrades, network partitions, counter wrap.
rows.observable: Monitoring-pipeline integrity, coverage, and time synchronization
rows.precise_data_objects: Collector/agent uptime, scrape interval, missed scrapes, restarts, config version, disabled fields, counter reset/wrap, time sync/NTP/PTP status, clock drift, append-only log hashes, signed batches, deletion attempts, access-control changes, coverage maps for GPUs/nodes/switches/racks/PDU, retention policy.
rows.primary_governance_function: Determines whether the absence of evidence is meaningful; tracks sensor coverage, gaps, resets, clock drift, configuration changes, and tampering.
rows.recommended_reporting_form: Coverage/gap/retention dashboard, signed hashes, and exception reports; raw agent logs to auditor.
rows.sensitivity: Medium: reveals monitoring architecture and weak points.

rows.best_cross_checks: Inventory deltas, attestation changes, monitoring gaps, BMC logs, power/cooling changes.
rows.key_value_ranges_encodings: Access events: 0+ per window. Rack-door open duration: seconds-hours. Maintenance tickets: 0+. Hardware delta: add/remove/swap. Firmware/BMC changes: 0+. Authorized/unauthorized enum. Temporal alignment with telemetry: yes/no.
rows.large_training_signature_interpretation: Not a training signal. Useful when coincident with unexplained capacity changes, telemetry gaps, power anomalies, or suspected off-ledger hardware operation.
rows.main_false_negatives_failure_modes: Incomplete logs, collusion, unmonitored cages, camera retention limits, remote tampering without physical access.
rows.main_false_positives: Normal maintenance, troubleshooting, cabling, vendor work, hardware failures.
rows.observable: Physical security, maintenance, and change-management records
rows.precise_data_objects: Badge access, rack-door sensors, camera log references, maintenance tickets, hardware install/remove/swap records, BMC/IPMI logins, firmware-change approvals, spare part/RMA movement, cabling changes, emergency access, operator override logs.
rows.primary_governance_function: Detects unauthorized hardware changes, sensor disabling, rack access, firmware changes, or maintenance events that could explain telemetry anomalies.
rows.recommended_reporting_form: Exception-based summaries and change approvals; raw personnel data only under narrow trigger.
rows.sensitivity: High: security posture, personnel movement, site layout.

rows.best_cross_checks: Attestation, GPU telemetry, scheduler idleness, power, monitoring integrity.
rows.key_value_ranges_encodings: Throughput ratio observed/expected: 0-1+. Latency inflation: 0-∞. Memory availability: 0-HBM GB. Probe pass/fail: enum. Sample randomness entropy: bits. Availability contention score: 0-1.
rows.large_training_signature_interpretation: Low available throughput or memory during supposedly idle windows can reveal hidden use. Probes indicate contention/availability, not necessarily training; they are most useful as spot checks or when other telemetry is distrusted.
rows.main_false_negatives_failure_modes: Predictable probes, scheduling around probes, workload migration, probe too weak/too infrequent, interference not allowed in production.
rows.main_false_positives: Benign co-tenancy, thermal/power caps, maintenance, background jobs, probe interference.
rows.observable: Active challenge probes and weak-trust telemetry tests
rows.precise_data_objects: Randomized proof-of-work-like parallel probes, sequential timing/VDF-like probes, GEMM/Tensor Core throughput probes, VRAM-residency/locality probes, probe schedule, expected-vs-observed throughput/latency, contention indicators, device-response signatures.
rows.primary_governance_function: Actively tests hidden utilization, available compute, memory residency, or contention when passive telemetry or host trust is weak.
rows.recommended_reporting_form: Randomized auditor-run spot checks with safety limits; publish only aggregate pass/fail/coverage.
rows.sensitivity: Medium: can disrupt workloads and expose performance baselines.

rows.best_cross_checks: Inventory, facility power/cooling, cloud region announcements, procurement, scheduler telemetry from monitored operators.
rows.category: Base capacity/discovery corroboration; weak activity signal
rows.key_value_ranges_encodings: Estimated IT power: 0+ MW with uncertainty interval. Building/rack count: 0+. Timeline: dates/months. Shipment count: 0+. Confidence: 0-1. Public disclosure status: none/partial/full. Location precision: site/region/country.
rows.large_training_signature_interpretation: Good for identifying capacity and construction timeline; weak for proving a particular run occurred in a particular week. Useful when telemetry claims contradict physical scale or when unmonitored clusters may exist.
rows.main_false_negatives_failure_modes: Indoor/underground or leased capacity, undisclosed shipments, inaccurate permits, multi-use facilities, poor imagery cadence.
rows.main_false_positives: Generic data centers, delayed/unused capacity, cloud regions not assigned to AI, public rumors.
rows.observable: External and out-of-band evidence: satellite, permits, utility, shipments, public disclosures
rows.precise_data_objects: Satellite/aerial imagery, construction progress, cooling infrastructure, utility interconnection and substation data, power permits, backup generators, chip shipments/procurement/customs/RMA, network peering/BGP, job postings/contracts/filings/press releases, leaks/whistleblower reports.
rows.primary_governance_function: Finds or corroborates large AI infrastructure outside the monitored telemetry boundary and sanity-checks claimed power/capacity.
rows.recommended_reporting_form: Public context plus confidential regulator corroboration; do not treat as sole compliance evidence.
rows.sensitivity: Varies; public sources low, utility/procurement data high.
